title: EIP-8477: Recent Block Bound Delegation Authorizations
description: Require delegation authorizations to bind to one of the preceding 256 execution block hashes.
author: Joseph Delong (@dangerousfood)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract Require every [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) authorization to sign an execution block number and its block header hash. An authorization may be applied only when the referenced block is one of the 256 immediate ancestors of the block including the transaction. Authorizations referencing older blocks, the current block, future blocks, or a different history are skipped. Legacy authorizations without a signed block reference are rejected after activation. This bounds the inclusion window of an unused authorization. It does not impose an expiry on an installed delegation. ## Motivation An unused delegation authorization can remain usable for an indefinite period if its account nonce remains unchanged. An authorization for a future nonce can also become usable later. Access to a previously signed authorization can therefore allow an attacker to install account code after the signer has stopped expecting that authorization to be used. A mandatory recent block reference limits this exposure independently of nonce advancement, signature storage policy, and relayer behavior. Once the referenced block falls outside the permitted ancestor window, the authorization cannot be applied on that chain history even if its nonce subsequently matches. The freshness condition must be enforced during native authorization processing. A deadline checked by delegate code or transaction calldata cannot prevent the protocol from first installing a delegation. Accepting legacy authorizations alongside the new format would leave previously signed authorizations outside the freshness requirement. ## Specification ### Parameters and definitions | Name | Value | | --- | --- | | `AUTHORIZATION_HISTORY_WINDOW` | `256` | | `SET_CODE_TX_TYPE` | `0x04`, unchanged | | `MAGIC` | `0x05`, unchanged | Let `B` be the execution block being processed and `N` its block number. For `0 <= b < N`, `ancestor_hash(B, b)` is the hash of the execution block header at number `b` on the ancestry of `B`. The hash is calculated using the header encoding applicable to that ancestor's fork. It is not a beacon block root, a transaction hash, or an arbitrary header supplied by the transaction sender. Unless changed below, all transaction validity, authorization processing, signature, nonce, gas, and delegation rules of EIP-7702 continue to apply. ### Authorization encoding Starting with the network upgrade activating this EIP, each entry in a type `0x04` transaction's `authorization_list` has exactly eight fields: ```text [ chain_id, address, nonce, anchor_block_number, anchor_block_hash, y_parity, r, s ] ``` The existing fields retain their EIP-7702 encodings and structural bounds. The additional fields are: - `anchor_block_number`: a canonically RLP-encoded unsigned integer satisfying `0 <= anchor_block_number < 2**256`. - `anchor_block_hash`: an RLP byte string of exactly 32 bytes. An incorrect field count, noncanonical encoding, incorrect field type, or violation of a structural bound makes the entire transaction invalid. A legacy six-field authorization entry is invalid after activation, including when mixed with eight-field entries. An absent anchor has no default value or fallback interpretation. Before activation, the legacy encoding remains in effect. Historical transactions are decoded and validated using the rules applicable to their inclusion block. ### Authorization signing digest The message used for authority recovery becomes: ```text authorization_digest = keccak256( MAGIC || rlp([ chain_id, address, nonce, anchor_block_number, anchor_block_hash ]) ) ``` Both anchor fields are covered by the authority's signature. Updating either field requires a new authorization signature. The outer transaction retains its existing field order and signing procedure: ```text outer_digest = keccak256( SET_CODE_TX_TYPE || rlp([ chain_id, nonce, max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas, gas_limit, destination, value, data, access_list, authorization_list ]) ) ``` The complete, extended authorization entries are included in this outer digest. ### Freshness validation Authorization processing occurs at the same point as in EIP-7702, after the outer sender's nonce has been incremented and before destination execution. Before signature recovery or any authority-specific state access for an entry, check, in order: 1. `anchor_block_number < N`. 2. `N - anchor_block_number <= AUTHORIZATION_HISTORY_WINDOW`. 3. `anchor_block_hash == ancestor_hash(B, anchor_block_number)`. The first check precedes subtraction. These rules admit exactly the ancestor heights in `[max(0, N - 256), N - 1]`. The parent is eligible. An ancestor exactly 256 blocks behind is eligible. An ancestor 257 blocks behind is ineligible. No anchor is eligible when `N == 0`. If any freshness check fails, stop processing that entry and continue with the next authorization. That entry performs no signature recovery, authority warming, delegation write, authority nonce increment, or authorization refund. The transaction sender still pays the authorization's intrinsic charge. If all freshness checks pass, process the entry under EIP-7702 using the new authorization digest. Freshness is necessary but does not replace any existing signature, chain ID, authority-code, or nonce check. The ancestor lookup is part of native transaction processing. It does not execute an EVM instruction or contract call, consume EVM execution gas, or add an account or storage key to an access set. Implementations must obtain the actual referenced ancestor hash; unavailable ancestor data must not be substituted with a sentinel hash. An expired or mismatched anchor is an authorization failure, not a transaction validity failure. Consequently, an otherwise valid transaction whose authorizations are all skipped may still execute its destination and succeed. Existing delegation on an authority is not removed by skipping an entry. ### Gas accounting This EIP adds no separate gas surcharge. EIP-7702's `PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT
